home.title: Sign Bitcoin with telephone tones, on a device you build yourself
home.lede: A signer that speaks DTMF, the beeps of a telephone keypad. A cheap microcontroller and a few parts from an electronics shop, or from the scrapyard, are enough.
home.urtones: It speaks ur-tones, an open way to send data as sound:
home.keypad_hint: Press a key: each is two tones at once, one from each group.

first.title: First time? Try this
first.1: On the signer, press OK until “Load seed”. In the wallet, {seed}.
first.2: Type on the signer the PIN the wallet shows, and check the fingerprint.
first.3: On the signer, “Sign PSBT”. In the wallet, {pay}. Check on the signer what the wallet shows, then hold OK.
first.4: In the wallet, {scan} the QR the signer shows.

card.seed_note_air: Through the air, with a PIN of 12 or more. A public test seed: never for real funds.
card.psbt_note_air: The signer will read you the same; at the end, hang up for a moment (R) to sign.
first.voice.1: Lift the handset and listen; press {hash} to go on.
first.voice.2: Seed: {one} then {two} (keypad) and {type}; or {one}, {one} (earpiece) and {seed} in the wallet, then type the PIN it shows.
first.voice.3: Sign: {one} and {pay} in the wallet. Listen to the review, {hash} after each part and, at the end, {flash} (a short hang-up).
first.voice.4: In the wallet, {listen}; then {hash} to hear the signature in the earpiece.
